title: Ganesha and the Race Around the World
bigQuestion: How can thinking in a new way help us?

story.title: The Race in the Garden
story.kicker: Two brothers race around the whole world, and one of them never leaves the garden.
paragraphs: Two brothers sit in a garden. One is Kartikeya. The other is Ganesha. Their parents are Shiva and Parvati. "Let's have a race," says their father.
"Go around the whole world," he says. "The first one back wins." Kartikeya jumps on his peacock. Whoosh! He flies away fast.
Ganesha rides a little mouse. The mouse is slow. Ganesha thinks and thinks. Then he stands up and walks around his mother and father.
"You are my whole world," Ganesha says. His parents smile. Ganesha wins the race. He never even left the garden! His brother is still flying.
story.think: Ganesha found a new way to win. Why did his parents like his answer?

lessons.title: The Elephant-Headed One
lessons.mainIdea: Ganesha has an elephant head, and many Hindus honor him.
reading: *Ganesha* has the head of an elephant. He has a big round belly. He often holds a sweet in one hand.
Many Hindus honor Ganesha. They love him very much. His parents are Shiva and Parvati. Hindus honor them too.

words.d: a deity with an elephant head, honored by many Hindus as the remover of obstacles

look.title: Ganesha in the Hall
look.text: Look at the murti by the front door. A murti is a sacred image. This one is Ganesha. He has big ears and a curled trunk. A small mouse sits at his feet.
look.prompt: What do you notice first about Ganesha?

check.q: What kind of head does Ganesha have?
check.why: Ganesha has the head of an elephant.
The stories say Ganesha's parents are Shiva and Parvati.
Hindus call a sacred image a murti.

lessons.title: Remover of Obstacles
lessons.mainIdea: Many Hindus pray to Ganesha before new beginnings.
reading: An obstacle is something in your way. Many Hindus call Ganesha the remover of obstacles.
So many Hindus pray to Ganesha before something new. It might be a new school year or a new home. It might be a trip.

words.d: something that is in your way
a name many Hindus give Ganesha

look.title: A New Beginning
look.text: Look at the family in their new home. Boxes are still on the floor. First, they set a small Ganesha murti on a shelf. They light a lamp near it.
look.prompt: Why might this family think of Ganesha first in a new home?

check.why: An obstacle is something that blocks your way.

check.q: What do many Hindus call Ganesha?
check.why: Many Hindus call Ganesha the remover of obstacles.

check.q: When do many Hindus pray to Ganesha?
check.why: Many Hindus pray to Ganesha before new beginnings.

lessons.title: Ganesha's Mouse
reading: Ganesha is big. But he rides a tiny mouse! The mouse is his helper. It goes everywhere with him.
Artists often paint the mouse at his feet. Some say the mouse shows that small things matter too.

words.d: a small animal; Ganesha's helper in the stories

look.title: Big and Small
look.text: Look at the painting. Ganesha is big and smiling. The mouse is very small. It looks up at Ganesha. It holds a sweet in its paws.
look.prompt: Why do you think a big Ganesha rides a small mouse?

check.why: In the stories, Ganesha rides a little mouse.

check.q: Where do artists often paint the mouse?
check.why: The mouse often sits at Ganesha's feet in pictures.

check.q: What do some say the mouse shows?
check.why: Some say the little mouse shows that small things matter.

lessons.title: Two Brothers
lessons.mainIdea: Ganesha and Kartikeya race around the world.
reading: Ganesha has a brother named Kartikeya. Kartikeya rides a fast peacock. Their parents give them a race.
"Go around the whole world," they say. Kartikeya flies off at once. Ganesha's mouse is slow. What can he do?

words.d: Ganesha's brother, who rides a peacock

look.title: Fast and Slow
look.text: Look at the two brothers. Kartikeya sits on a peacock. Its bright tail feathers spread wide. Ganesha sits on a little mouse. The mouse takes tiny steps.
look.prompt: Who do you think will be faster? Why?

check.why: Kartikeya is Ganesha's brother.
Kartikeya rides a fast peacock.
The brothers race around the whole world.

lessons.title: My Parents Are My World
lessons.mainIdea: Ganesha walks around his parents and says they are his world.
reading: Ganesha thinks hard. Then he walks slowly around his mother and father. He goes all the way around them.
"You are my world," he says. His parents are happy. They say Ganesha wins. He thought in a new way.

words.d: to show great respect and love

look.title: Ganesha's Answer
look.text: Ganesha walks around his parents. He says that going around them is like going around the whole world. His parents agree he has won.
look.cite: Retold from the Shiva Purana, Rudra Samhita, Kumara Khanda, and from family tellings
look.prompt: What does Ganesha mean when he says his parents are his world?

check.why: Ganesha walks around his parents, Shiva and Parvati.
Ganesha says his parents are his world.
His parents say Ganesha wins.

lessons.title: Ganesha's Festival
lessons.mainIdea: Many Hindus celebrate Ganesha at Ganesh Chaturthi.
reading: Ganesh Chaturthi is Ganesha's festival. It comes in late summer. Many Hindu families bring home a Ganesha murti.
They offer flowers and sweets. They sing songs. Many cities have big parades. Families in Illinois celebrate it too.

look.title: Sweets for Ganesha
look.text: Look at the plate. It has round sweets called modak. Many families say Ganesha loves modak. A child sets the plate near the murti with care.
look.prompt: Why do families set out foods they say Ganesha loves?

check.why: Ganesh Chaturthi honors Ganesha.
Families offer flowers and sweets.

check.q: What sweet do many say Ganesha loves?
check.why: Many families say Ganesha loves modak.

lessons.title: Thinking in a New Way
lessons.mainIdea: Ganesha's story helps children think about new ideas and honoring parents.
reading: Kartikeya was fast. Ganesha was clever. He found a new way to solve the problem.
Families tell this story to talk about two things. Think in a new way. Honor the people who care for you.

words.d: good at thinking of smart ideas

look.title: A Tricky Problem
look.text: Look at the girl at the table. Her puzzle piece does not fit. She stops. She turns the piece around. Click! Now it fits.
look.prompt: How is the girl like Ganesha in the race?

choices: He thought in a new way
check.why: Ganesha was clever and found a new way.

choices: Good at thinking of smart ideas
check.why: Clever means good at thinking of smart ideas.

check.q: What else does the story teach?
choices: Honor the people who care for you
check.why: Ganesha honors his parents in the story.
